title: Employee Lifecycle Operating Manual
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This operating manual describes the end-to-end employee lifecycle at Redwood Inference: candidate sourcing and hiring, pre-boarding and first-week onboarding, role expectations and promotion pathways, benefits and perks, internal tooling access, lateral moves, and offboarding. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, new hires, and engineering managers who run rotations.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single, practical reference that combines process, templates, ownership, and tooling for the full employee lifecycle.
- Apply to all US, EMEA, and APAC hires unless a regional policy overrides a specific benefit or compliance rule.

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops).
- Secondary owners: Hiring Managers (owner_team: engineering/product), IT & Security for access provisioning.
- Escalation path: People Ops -> Head of People Ops -> COO.

1) Hiring and candidate experience
Intro: Use Greenhouse as the single source of truth for candidate workflow and scorecards. Follow the interview loop below to ensure consistent evaluation.

Interview loop (standard for IC / engineering):
1. Recruiter screen (30 min) – cultural fit, motivation, logistics.
2. Technical screen (45 min) – system design or coding depending on level.
3. Take-home or paired exercise (where applicable).
4. Onsite / loop (4–5 interviews, 60 min each): design, deep dive, product sense, manager, and bar-raiser.
5. Debrief and hire decision.

Hiring checklist (pre-offer):
- Background checks scheduled (if required by role/region).
- Compensation calibration with People Ops and Finance.
- Offer letter drafted using standard template (GH: /templates/offer-standard).
- Manager confirms onboarding buddy and first-week schedule.

Offer and acceptance: Send offer via Greenhouse-generated PDF and include: start date, manager, team orientation details, first-week agenda, remote equipment plan, 30/60/90 expectations.

2) Pre-boarding (2–4 weeks before start)
- People Ops creates HR record (Workday) and triggers Okta provision.
- IT orders laptop & peripherals; procurement SLA: 7 business days for US, 14 business days EMEA/APAC.
- Manager sends welcome packet with first-week agenda and buddy assignment.
- New hire completes required e-learning (security basics, code of conduct) before day 1.

3) Day 1 and first week: sample schedule
- Day 1: 09:30 welcome (People Ops), 10:30 accounts & SSO setup (IT), 13:00 team lunch (virtual/in-person), 15:00 product overview.
- Week 1: role-specific onboarding sessions, compliance training, assigned small starter task (<= 8 hrs) to land productive ramp.

Quick access checklist (Day 1):
- Okta / single sign-on configured
- Email and Slack active
- Miro/Jira/Confluence permissions verified
- Github repo access granted and PAT guidance provided

Sample CLI for engineering access request (manager-initiated):
- Create an internal access ticket: "ops-tool create-access --user a.kapoor --roles coder,ci-runner --reason 'onboarding'"
- For cloud project access (example):
  gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference-prod \
    --member='user:alice@example.com' \
    --role='roles/viewer'

4) Role expectations and career ladders
Overview: Each function maintains a leveled ladder (IC and managerial tracks). Managers must publish role-specific rubrics during hiring and at promotion time.

Promotion rubric (summary):
- Required artifacts:
  - Updated competency self-assessment
  - 360 feedback collected via People Ops template
  - Evidence of impact (PRs, release notes, customer outcomes)
- Criteria to evaluate:
  1. Scope increase: impact beyond current team or feature area.
  2. Technical/functional depth: demonstrates craft and tradeoffs.
  3. Influence: mentorship, cross-team coordination, shaping product direction.
  4. Consistency: contributions sustained over 6–12 months.

Competency snapshot (example table):
| Level | Scope | Expected outcomes | Promotion signal |
|-------|-------|-------------------|------------------|
| IC2   | Owns single feature | Delivers on feature roadmap, clear tickets | Repeated reliably across 6 months |
| IC3   | Multi-feature / small service | Leads design, mentors peers, measurable KPIs | Significant impact on product metric; scales work |
| IC4   | Cross-team area | Shapes architecture, leads cross-team projects | Recognized as a subject matter expert |

Manager training and expectations:
- All managers complete Manager Essentials within 60 days of assuming role.
- Managers must set clear 30/60/90 plans with employees and review progress monthly.

5) Benefits and perks (high level)
Summary: Redwood offers competitive benefits that include health coverage, 401(k) or local equivalent, parental leave, flexible time off, learning stipend, home-office stipend, and commuter benefits where applicable. Specific eligibility and plan details are in Workday.

Benefits quick table:
| Program | Eligibility | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-------|
| Health insurance | Full-time, post-probation | Multiple plans; enrollment in first 30 days |
| Parental leave | Full-time | 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (US policy) |
| Learning stipend | All employees | $1,200/year for conferences/courses |
| Home-office stipend | New hires | $500 one-time; additional ergonomic budget via People Ops |

Perk highlights:
- Monthly wellness stipend (local currency equivalent)
- Quarterly hackday and team offsite support
- Referral bonus paid after 90 days of hire

6) Internal tools and access patterns
Primary tooling matrix (ownership and notes):
- HRIS: Workday (People Ops)
- ATS: Greenhouse (People Ops/Recruiting)
- SSO: Okta (IT/Security)
- Password manager: 1Password (IT/Security)
- Communication: Slack (All)
- Code repo: Github Enterprise (Eng)
- Ticketing: Jira (Eng/Product)
- Documentation: Confluence (All)
- Cloud console: GCP (Infra team manages project namespace)

Access request lifecycle:
1. Manager opens access request ticket in ServiceNow/IT portal with role code and justification.
2. IT verifies procurement and assigns hardware.
3. Okta group sync grants access to tooling within 24 business hours (priority: 48 hours during ramps).

Common templates (copy into ticket):
- Subject: "New hire access request: [Name] – [Team] – [Start Date]"
- Body: "Name: 
Role: 
Start date: 
Required groups: github:coder, jira:team-X, gcp:dev-project-A"

7) Lateral moves, rotations, and sabbaticals
- Lateral moves should be notified to People Ops at least 30 days before the target start.
- Rotation duration: typically 3–6 months; sponsoring manager defines clear goals.
- Sabbatical policy: Eligible after 3 years of continuous service; reference People Ops policy for approval workflow.

8) Offboarding and knowledge handover
Offboarding checklist (manager + People Ops):
1. Confirm final date and communicate to payroll and benefits.
2. Knowledge transfer plan: at least one shadow week and written runbook for critical responsibilities.
3. Revoke access: trigger automated Okta deprovisioning (day-of) and rotate shared credentials.
4. Exit interview scheduled by People Ops.

Data retention and security notes:
- Managers must ensure ownership transfer of any customer accounts or keys before offboard.
- For Private deployment engineers, rotate production creds and report to Security within 24 hours.

9) Metrics and SLAs for People Ops services
- New hire full provisioning SLA: 5 business days (US), 10 business days (EMEA/APAC).
- Offer-to-accept cycle time target: median 7 days.
- First-week enablement rate: target 95% of hires meet Quick access checklist by EOD Day 1.

10) Templates and quick examples
Manager 30/60/90 outline (paste into calendar invite):
- 30 days: learn codebase, ship a small ticket, meet cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: lead a small design, mentor another engineer, improve a CI/CD flow.
- 90 days: own a feature end-to-end with metrics and post-mortem.

Sample welcome Slack message:
"Please welcome @new-hire (Role, Team). Start date: 2025-04-01. Buddy: @buddy. First 1:1 with manager scheduled on Day 2. Please say hi and share any docs that will help them get up to speed."

FAQ (selection):
Q: Who signs off on promotions?
A: Manager + peer review + People Ops calibration committee.

Q: How do I request a laptop upgrade?
A: Submit hardware request with manager approval; upgrades are reviewed quarterly.

Appendix: Templates, links, and references
- Offer templates: /templates/offer-standard
- Promotion packet checklist: /templates/promotion-packet
- Manager training: /learning/manager-essentials
- Security onboarding: /security/new-joiner

Revision history:
- 2024-09-15: created by Aisha Kapoor (People Ops)
- 2025-03-10: updated procurement SLAs, added CLI example and rotation policy

If anything in this manual conflicts with a legal or regional policy, the regional policy supersedes. For questions or suggested edits, contact people-ops@redwood.com.
